title: Hassan ibn Thabit
hookLine: the poet of the Prophet ﷺ, who defended him in verse

cards: Lines of verse mocking the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, are passing from mouth to mouth. Not arrows. Rhymes.
A sharp line is easy to remember, and it can make a man look like a fool to people who have never met him. So what does a community do when it's attacked in verse? Ignore it?
Answer with force? Or find a poet of its own. Today: Hassan ibn Thabit, who answered.

teach.b: Hassan was a man of Medina and a poet. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the Prophet's charge to him. In one report, the Prophet tells Hassan to answer the poets who were mocking, and says that Gabriel is with him.

teach.h: SUPPORT HIM WITH THE HOLY SPIRIT.
teach.b: In another: answer on my behalf, and he prays, O God, support him with the Holy Spirit. A poet, told his verses had help from heaven. Then the pulpit.
Aisha reports, in the collections of Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, that the Prophet had a pulpit set up for Hassan in the mosque, where Hassan would stand and defend the Prophet in verse.
Poetry, in the place of prayer, on a raised step, with permission. Not everyone was comfortable with that. Bukhari tells a scene after the Prophet's death.
Umar passes Hassan reciting in the mosque and shows his disapproval. Hassan doesn't back down. I used to recite in here, he says, when someone better than you was present.
Then he turns to Abu Hurayrah and asks, by God, whether he heard the Prophet say: answer on my behalf, O God, support him with the Holy Spirit.
Abu Hurayrah says yes. Hassan took the weapon being used against the community and turned it into a defense, with the Prophet's blessing, in the open. Words can wound.
His answer was more words, placed where everyone could hear.

how: Muslims remember Hassan ibn Thabit as the poet of the Prophet, from reports in Bukhari and in Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi that a pulpit was set up for him in the mosque, and some Muslims still recite poems in praise of the Prophet today.

games.q: you are Hassan, reciting poetry in the mosque. Umar walks past and shows he disapproves. what do you do?
o: say you recited here before someone better, and ask a witness.
leave the mosque and recite outside.
games.why: Bukhari says Hassan answered that he had recited there when the Prophet was present, and asked Abu Hurayrah to confirm the Prophet's words. Abu Hurayrah said yes.

practice: Bring to mind someone or something that deserves honoring: a friend talked about unfairly, a teacher, a place you love, or, if you pray, God.
Find four short lines in praise, slowly, one for each breath; they don't need to rhyme, and true lines are better than clever ones.

wordCard.voice: Hassan, the poet of Medina given a pulpit in the mosque to answer the Prophet's critics in verse, with the Prophet's own blessing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Hassan, son of Thabit, the poet of the Prophet.

carryVoice: Your line: the poet's pulpit. Verse, answered with more verse, in the open. Until tomorrow.
